question: Does a fully logged replication from the public rdrobust_senate data reproduce the headline sharp regression-discontinuity estimate of the US Senate incumbency advantage reported by Calonico, Cattaneo, Farrell and Titiunik (2017) (point estimate and robust bias-corrected 95% confidence interval), and does the estimate survive pre-specified falsification checks (a density test of the running variable and a test on a predetermined covariate or placebo cutoffs)?
hypotheses: H1 (replication): the replicated point estimate and robust bias-corrected 95% CI match the published values (verified by the Scout from the source, not recalled) within a tolerance fixed at the design gate from the published rounding and software differences. Reported per target (point, CI low, CI high) as reproduced or not.

H2 (falsification; pre-specified, judged on the fixed tests): the density test of the margin of victory at zero does not reject continuity at the 5% level, and the pre-specified predetermined-covariate or placebo-cutoff tests show no discontinuity at the 5% level (with the multiplicity of the placebo tests stated in advance). A rejection is reported as such and qualifies the replication; it is not explained away.
contribution: A logged, rerunnable replication of a standard regression-discontinuity estimate with its falsification checks fixed before any outcome analysis. This workspace is also the crew's low-cost trial: every role subagent, including the Reviewer, runs on Claude Haiku 5.5, so its cost and quality can be compared with the other gallery papers.

tasks.title: The published estimate (CCFT 2017, Stata Journal 17(2); data of Cattaneo, Frandsen and Titiunik 2015), its exact specification and software version; prior replications and the falsification checks used in that literature

disclosures: 2026-11-20 (question stage, PI): By the human's choice this workspace is a low-cost trial. Every role subagent, including the Reviewer, runs on Claude Haiku 5.5; the PI session runs on Claude Opus 5.5. Cost is measured with crew/scripts/usage.py and compared with the other gallery papers.
